newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds steady, await UK monetary meeting.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds steady, await UK monetary meeting.

text.p: Irish bonds started on a steady note on Tuesday but worries about currency market turbulence and the meeting between Britain's new Chancellor Gordon Brown and Bank of England Governor Eddie George were expected to keep a cap on the market, dealers said.

"People are keeping an eye on the George/Brown meeting to see whether we get a 50 basis point hike...Initially people talked about 25 bp but expectations have moved into the 50 bp levels," one dealer said.
Brown brought forward his monthly monetary meeting with George to today. A statement is expected around 1000 GMT.
Gains in other European debt markets and an early infusion of cash by Irish authorities early on Tuesday helped reverse an early sell-off in the short end of the market, one trader said.

But the Irish pound, up against both sterling and the mark in early trade, continued to give concern, particularly with the looming threat of a possible British rate rise, one trader said. Others noted that Irish-German interest rate differentials could prevent further speculative pressure on the pound.
Dealers said there were few concerns about expectations that commercial banks would raise mortgage rates after the central bank's tightening last week.
"The banks are holding off at present but we think they are just staving off the inevitable. It's pretty much priced into the market and we don't see much impact," one trader said.
Traders said the market was not concerned about Thursday's release of Irish consumer price data for April.
At 0935 GMT, the benchmark 10-year Irish bond was down five pence at 108.55 for an annual yield of 6.72 percent.
